title: Leaner Training, Lower Leakage: Revisiting Memorization in LLM Fine-Tuning with LoRA
abstract: arXiv:2506.20856v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Memorization in large language models (LLMs) makes them vulnerable to data extraction attacks. While pre-training memorization has been extensively studied, fewer works have explored its impact in fine-tuning, particularly for LoRA fine-tuning, a widely adopted parameter-efficient method.   In this work, we re-examine memorization in fine-tuning and uncover a surprising divergence from prior findings across different fine-tuning strategies. Factors such as model scale and data duplication, which strongly influence memorization in pre-training and full fine-tuning, do not follow the same trend in LoRA fine-tuning. Using a more relaxed similarity-based memorization metric, we demonstrate that LoRA significantly reduces memorization risks compared to full fine-tuning, while still maintaining strong task performance.

translated_title: 更精简的训练，更低的泄露：用LoRA重新审视大语言模型微调中的记忆化现象
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）中的记忆化现象使其容易受到数据提取攻击。虽然预训练阶段的记忆化已被广泛研究，但很少有工作探讨其在微调中的影响，特别是对于LoRA微调——一种被广泛采用的参数高效方法。在本工作中，我们重新审视了微调中的记忆化现象，并发现了与以往研究在不同微调策略上的惊人差异。模型规模和数据重复等在预训练和全量微调中强烈影响记忆化的因素，在LoRA微调中并不遵循相同的趋势。通过使用更宽松的基于相似性的记忆化度量，我们证明了与全量微调相比，LoRA显著降低了记忆化风险，同时仍保持了强大的任务性能。
tldr: 本研究重新审视了LLM微调中的记忆化现象，发现LoRA微调相比全量微调能显著降低记忆化和数据泄露风险，且模型规模和数据重复等因素在LoRA微调中的影响与预训练和全量微调不同。
en_tdlr: LoRA fine-tuning significantly reduces memorization risks compared to full fine-tuning while maintaining strong task performance, and factors like model scale and data duplication do not follow the same memorization trends in LoRA as in pre-training and full fine-tuning.
